+Gloss: The ring ℂ[y]/(yʳ+1) of complex polynomials of degree below r, r a power of two, in which yʳ = −1 so that multiplication wraps negacyclically.
+The symbols in this page's heading denote (say so on the page):
+- $y$ (polynomial variable): The indeterminate of the ring, whose powers act as roots of unity because y to the r equals −1.
+- $r$ (record length): The number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record, a power of two.
+## Where the argument relies on this page

+- A layer of normalized butterflies $H_0$ on the same bit position of $D\le d$ address chunks of an array of polynomial records can be applied, exactly and then truncated once, in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time for a fixed $\lambda'<1$. (on [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md))

+- Normalized cyclic convolution of arrays of $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ records on power-of-two axes of total size $T$ can be approximated within $\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$ at cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}+\log(rp)])$. (on [Convolution over the polynomial ring](synthetic-convolution.md))

+- The decimation-in-frequency recursion with synthetic roots $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$ computes $B_tF_t^-$ (frequency $j$ stored at slot $\operatorname{rev}(j)$), and the reversed recursion computes $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$. (on [Synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md))

+- Each pointwise product $Q_p(fg/r)$ in $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ is computed exactly by signed Kronecker substitution with four calls to the established multiplier, in $O(rp\log(rp))$ time. (on [Signed Kronecker substitution](kronecker-packing.md))

+- Multiplying coefficient $k$ of the last axis by $\zeta^k$, $\zeta=e^{\pi i/r}$, turns normalized complex cyclic convolution on power-of-two axes into convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, and untwisting recovers the cyclic wrap with the correct sign. (on [Coefficient phase twist](phase-twist.md))
+## Pages that build on this one

+- Synthetic roots of unity: Powers of y in ℂ[y]/(yʳ+1), such as ω_t = y^{2r/t}, which serve as roots of unity and act on a record by a signed cyclic shift of its coefficient list instead of a multiplication.

+- Signed Kronecker substitution: Multiplying polynomials with signed integer coefficients by evaluating them at a large power of two, multiplying the resulting integers with an established multiplier, and reading coefficients back by centered residues.

+- Simultaneous butterfly layer: A procedure applying H₀ on the same bit position of up to d address chunks of an array of polynomial records at once, in O(V d^{λ′}) time for a fixed λ′ < 1, evaluated exactly and truncated once.

+- Coefficient phase twist: Multiplying the k-th coefficient of the last cyclic axis by ζ^k with ζ = e^{πi/r}, which turns cyclic convolution of length r into multiplication modulo yʳ + 1 and is undone afterwards.

+- "one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two." (paper)

+  > Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients. Our starting point is the Gaussian-resampling reduction of Harvey and van der Hoeven \cite{HarveyHoeven2021}: it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two. After a further conversion to convolution, one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two. Powers of $y$ then serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes, and multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list. These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and Nussbaumer~\cite{NussbaumerQuandalle1978,Nussbaumer1980}.

+- "and proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth" (paper)

+  > Sch\"onhage and Strassen proved in 1971 that two $n$-bit integers can be multiplied in $O(n\log n\log\log n)$ time on a multitape Turing machine, and proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth \cite[Section~1]{SchonhageStrassen1971}. After a sequence of improvements, Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper bound~\cite{HarveyHoeven2021}. We obtain a strict power saving in the logarithmic factor, in the same fixed finite-tape model. The algorithm uses linear combinations of intermediate data to reduce the cost of both address rearrangement and Fourier-transform layers.
+- "Sch\"onhage and Strassen conjectured $n\log n$ as the optimal order of multiplication cost" (paper)

+  > Sch\"onhage and Strassen conjectured $n\log n$ as the optimal order of multiplication cost~\cite[Section~1]{SchonhageStrassen1971}. In the present fixed-tape model, an eventual lower bound for every multiplication machine means that, for each fixed machine $A$, there are constants $c_A>0$ and $N_A$ such that $T_A(n)\ge c_A n\lg n$ whenever $n\ge N_A$. Its negation requires one machine satisfying $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$. The power saving proved here gives a limit of zero through all input lengths, which is a stronger conclusion.

+## Where the argument relies on this page

+- The normalized transforms $F_t^\pm$ over $\mathcal R_r$ are contractions computed by radix-two butterflies, and the stored frequency order is consumed exactly by the inverse. (on [Synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-polynomial-transform.md))

+- The normalized convolution $\mathcal M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/T$ over $\mathcal R_r$ is a bilinear contraction, computed from the retained layout with error below $\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$. (on [Normalized convolution over the polynomial ring](normalized-ring-convolution.md))
+- The exact Gaussian integer numerators of $fg$ are computed and the rounded value $Q_p(fg/r)$ is returned in time $O(rp\log(rp))$.
+- The power-of-two complex convolution is obtained from the synthetic convolution by a phase twist $x_d\mapsto\zeta y$ with $\zeta=e^{\pi i/r}$. (on [Phase twist to negacyclic wrap](phase-twist.md))
+## Pages that build on this one

+- Signed Kronecker packing: Encoding a polynomial with signed integer coefficients as a single integer by placing the coefficients at fixed bit spacing, so that one integer product computes the polynomial product.

+- Synthetic polynomial transform: A transform over the polynomial ring in which the roots of unity are powers of y, so that multiplying by a root is a signed shift of a coefficient list, computed with radix-two butterflies.

+- Phase twist to negacyclic wrap: A phase multiplication of the last cyclic coordinate that turns the cyclic wrap-around into the negative wrap of the polynomial ring, so that the original cyclic product is recovered once the twist is removed.

+  > Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients. Our starting point is the Gaussian-resampling reduction of Harvey and van der Hoeven \cite{HarveyHoeven2021}: it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two. After a further conversion to convolution, one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two. Powers of $y$ then serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes, and multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list. These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and Nussbaumer~\cite{NussbaumerQuandalle1978,Nussbaumer1980}.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. - artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

+## Pages that build on this one

+- Polynomial roots of unity: The observation that powers of y in the polynomial ring are roots of unity whose multiplication is a signed shift, so a transform over the ring can use them as twiddle factors.

+- Phase twist of the last coordinate: The isomorphism from the cyclic group algebra of length r to the polynomial ring that sends x to ζy with ζ = e^(πi/r), implemented by multiplying coefficient k by ζ^k and undone by multiplying by ζ^(−k).

+- Signed coefficient packing: Evaluating two integer polynomials at a large base 2^(4p) so that one exact integer product yields all coefficient products, with signed carries recovered by centered residues; it is a signed form of Kronecker substitution.

+- Normalized polynomial-ring product: The normalized product f g / r of two disk-grid polynomials in the polynomial ring, computed exactly by signed packing into four integer products and returned truncated to the grid.

+  > Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients. Our starting point is the Gaussian-resampling reduction of Harvey and van der Hoeven \cite{HarveyHoeven2021}: it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two. After a further conversion to convolution, one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two. Powers of $y$ then serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes, and multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list. These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and Nussbaumer~\cite{NussbaumerQuandalle1978,Nussbaumer1980}.
